fallback.law: Some privacy laws require websites to ask before using cookies that aren't essential to how the site works.

EEA.law: European privacy law, under the ePrivacy Directive and the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR), requires websites to ask before storing cookies that aren't essential on your device.

GB.law: The UK's Privacy and Electronic Communications Regulations (PECR) and UK GDPR require websites to ask before storing most cookies that aren't essential on your device.

CH.law: Switzerland's Federal Act on Data Protection (FADP) requires websites to be clear about how they use your personal data and gives you a say in that use.

BR.law: Brazil's General Data Protection Law (LGPD) requires a legal basis, such as your consent, before a website uses your personal data.

CA-QC.law: Quebec's privacy law, as updated by Law 25, requires technology that can identify, locate or profile you to stay off until you choose to turn it on.

US-CA.law: California's privacy laws, including the California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA), give you the right to know about and opt out of the sale and sharing of your personal information.
